evidence.title: 'Get your house in order': IMF chief's stark warning for France over surging bond yields

occurrences.checkable_against: French national accounts and economic growth data
occurrences.quote_span: "The French economy is growing," she said.
occurrences.speaker: Kristalina Georgieva
occurrences.subject: France public finances

occurrences.checkable_against: French government budget proposals and parliamentary records
occurrences.quote_span: The movement – which has seen young people across the country demonstrate discontent with long study days, teacher shortages and rundown schools – comes as the French government seeks to win over a politically fractured parliament and convince lawmakers to agree to tens of billions of euros worth of spending cuts.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: France public finances

occurrences.checkable_against: Bond-market yield data, inflation data, interest-rate data, government debt data, and CNBC interview transcript
occurrences.quote_span: "Bond markets respond to fundamentals, and the fundamentals have changed," she added. "Inflation is up, interest rates are up, government debt is high. Bond markets are looking for signal that the government borrowing is going to be contained, and we are encouraging governments please send the signal because otherwise we may we may see further climbs up."
occurrences.speaker: Kristalina Georgieva
occurrences.subject: France public finances

occurrences.quote_span: She noted that since the Covid-19 pandemic, populations had become accustomed to governments "running to the rescue" of people and businesses when a shock occurs.

occurrences.quote_span: "And I think we need to remember that, [compared] to the previous time, we have a much more mature system in Europe. We have the strength of the European Central Bank. We have other instruments that Europe has developed to protect against financial stability risks."

occurrences.subject: France public finances

occurrences.checkable_against: CNBC interview transcript or recording with IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva
occurrences.quote_span: The head of the International Monetary Fund had a blunt message to the French government in a CNBC interview on Wednesday: bring your finances under control.

occurrences.subject: France public finances

occurrences.checkable_against: French and Italian government bond yield market data
occurrences.quote_span: Investors now demand a higher yield than they do for bonds issued by the Italian government, with French 10-year bond yields rising by more than 100 basis points since the start of the year.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: France public finances

occurrences.checkable_against: CNBC interview transcript and French fiscal plans
occurrences.quote_span: She noted that there is a "very clear recognition in France that deficit needs to be brought under 5%."
occurrences.speaker: Kristalina Georgieva
occurrences.subject: France public finances

occurrences.checkable_against: European Commission excessive deficit procedure documents for France
occurrences.quote_span: France is subject to the EU's excessive deficit procedure, with the bloc recommending the country bring its national deficit closer to a reference value of 3%.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: France public finances

occurrences.checkable_against: CNBC interview transcript or recording with IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva
occurrences.quote_span: "What we see in France is a complication of, on one side, the consequence of borrowing shock after shock after shock, climbing on this staircase that does not lead to heaven, and on the other side, a political dynamic scene in France that creates more difficulties for the finance ministry to put a clear path for tightening," IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva told CNBC's Lisa Kim on the sidelines of an event in Singapore.
occurrences.speaker: Kristalina Georgieva
occurrences.subject: France public finances

occurrences.quote_span: Political instability in France has put pressure on the country's government bonds, known as OATs.
